test_title: PYST 23: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I - GA (Held On: 14 Jun, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: The Great Plains of India were primarily formed due to the deposition by which of the following rivers?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Indus, Ganga and Brahmaputra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Great Plains of India are an extensive flat landmass stretching across northern India, formed primarily due to the deposition of sediments carried by the rivers **Indus, Ganga, and Brahmaputra**.
 
• These plains are also known as the Indo-Gangetic Plains and are one of the most fertile regions in the world due to rich alluvial soil deposited by the rivers.
 
• The sediment deposition process began millions of years ago when the Himalayas were formed, leading to erosion and transportation of materials downstream.
 
• The plains cover approximately 7 lakh square kilometers across northern and eastern India, including parts of Pakistan and Bangladesh.
 
• The rivers provided the necessary water and nutrients for agriculture, making the region a hub of ancient civilizations like the Indus Valley Civilization.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Alluvial Soil:**

 
 
• Alluvial soil is formed due to the deposition of sediments by rivers and is rich in minerals like potash, phosphoric acid, and lime.
 
• It is ideal for growing crops such as wheat, rice, sugarcane, and pulses.
 
 
 
• **Indus River System:**
 
 
• The Indus River originates from Tibet and flows through India and Pakistan, contributing significantly to sediment deposition.
 
• It has several tributaries, including Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Beas, and Sutlej.
 
 
 
• **Ganga River System:**
 
 
• The Ganga River originates from the Gangotri Glacier in the Himalayas and flows through northern India and Bangladesh.
 
• Major tributaries include Yamuna, Ghaghara, Gandak, and Kosi.
 
 
 
• **Brahmaputra River System:**
 
 
• The Brahmaputra River originates from Tibet and flows through northeastern India and Bangladesh.
 
• Its basin is one of the richest biodiversity hotspots in the world.
 
 
 
• **Importance of the Great Plains:**
 
 
• The region supports a large population due to its fertile soil and abundant water resources.
 
• It plays a crucial role in India's agricultural economy, contributing significantly to food production.
